      "Fine-scale groundwater recharge dynamics without coupling to PFLOTRAN"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 6,
  "n_justification": "The dominant control is the 352-1977 m elevation gradient (snow-vs-rain partitioning), so columns are stratified into low/mid/high elevation bands, with two soil-texture contrasts at mid-elevation and additional coverage where SNOTEL and USGS wells provide validation. Six columns span the elevation-forcing-soil factorial economically while each maps to at least one observational constraint.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "NAC_low_valley", "lat": 46.60, "lon": -120.55, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},

feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: precipitation, runoff, ET, and recharge partitioning are all diagnosable from ELM single-column water-balance outputs, and runoff/SWE/water-table can be validated observationally; ET cannot be directly validated (no flux towers) and is constrained only via closure.
answerable: Long-term partitioning of P into surface+subsurface runoff, total ET, and deep recharge (QCHARGE) per elevation/soil archetype
Elevation control on partitioning via a snow-dominated to rain-dominated gradient
SWE seasonality and magnitude validated against 6 SNOTEL stations
Simulated runoff/drainage compared to USGS stream-gauge daily records (where available)
Water-table depth (ZWT) compared against USGS well observations
not_answerable: Direct validation of ET fluxes (no flux towers in domain)
Fully spatially distributed basin routing / streamflow aggregation (single-column ELM has no lateral routing; gauge comparison is qualitative per representative column)
Fine-scale groundwater recharge dynamics without coupling to PFLOTRAN

parsed.n_justification: The dominant control is the 352-1977 m elevation gradient (snow-vs-rain partitioning), so columns are stratified into low/mid/high elevation bands, with two soil-texture contrasts at mid-elevation and additional coverage where SNOTEL and USGS wells provide validation. Six columns span the elevation-forcing-soil factorial economically while each maps to at least one observational constraint.
assumptions: A 200-400 year accelerated + final spin-up recycling 1980-2018 forcing is run before the transient simulation to equilibrate soil moisture, snowpack, and water table.
Single-column ELM has no lateral routing, so QRUNOFF+QDRAI is treated as local runoff generation and compared qualitatively (per-area) against USGS gauge unit-discharge rather than routed streamflow.
Deep recharge is approximated by QCHARGE (flux to unconfined aquifer); PFLOTRAN coupling is optional for refined subsurface flux.
Column point locations are chosen as elevation-band representatives near SNOTEL/well sites; surface parameters (PFT, soil, elevation) are set from gridded datasets at each point.
ET is evaluated only through water-balance closure (P = ET + runoff + recharge + dSWE/dt + dStorage) because no flux-tower observations exist.
Forcing is downscaled/lapse-corrected to each column elevation to preserve the snow-rain gradient.
